title: Lusin's theorem for Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n with a closed set, sets of infinite measure allowed (step 2 of Simon's proof of Ch. 2, 1.5)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let Y be a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra containing every open set. Let g : ℝ^n → Y be measurable, where ℝ^n = Euclid n carries its Borel σ-algebra. Let B ⊆ ℝ^n be measurable, possibly with L^n(B) = ∞, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that g is continuous on C (ContinuousOn g C) and L^n(B ∖ C) < ε, where L^n = volume.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (g : Euclid n → Y) (B : Set (Euclid n)), Measurable g → MeasurableSet B → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ C : Set (Euclid n), C ⊆ B ∧ IsClosed C ∧ ContinuousOn g C ∧ volume (B \ C) < ε
